text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A captured raider says the helicopter in which the Samburu district commissioner and two army officers were killed last month was brought down by a bullet and not a rocket.
- Kenya police shoot dead four suspected gangsters who allegedly raped an elderly woman and terrorised two villages in Kiambu district.
- President Daniel arap Moi flies to Zaire for a meeting with President Mobutu Sese Seko.
- Seven opposition members of parliament claim there is a plot to start fresh tribal clashes in the country before this year's general election.
- Paul Muite, opposition member of parliament for Kikuyu, urges the government to take a bold move to protect members of the Turkana community from attacks by bandits and cattle rustlers.
- Two suspected thieves who stole electronic goods from a house in Kalifi are lynched.
- Three gangsters are lynched to death by an angry crowd while their accomplice is shot dead by the police.
- The new police commissioner Duncan Wachira takes a tough stance in the administration of the police force.
- Twenty-eight head of cattle stolen from Samburu area late last year are recovered and one suspected cattle rustler is arrested by a security team.
- A variety of sources and eyewitness accounts say sanctions including a crucial oil embargo imposed on Burundi last July 31 are being evaded.
- As Tanzania prepares to face the Paris club of creditors, a rare controversy erupts over how much Tanzania owes Russia in foreign debt.

- A bruising East African trade dispute breaks out as Kenya protests against Uganda's extension of a ban on meat products from Europe to include Kenya, Tanzania and other neighbouring countries. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
